summary.headline: The Select Board denied Freddie Gillespie reappointment to the Open Space Preservation Commission, approved $30,000 for wastewater planning, and set Town Meeting dates.
summary.summary: At its June 16, 2026 meeting, the Select Board filled a Library Board of Trustees vacancy and denied reappointment of long-serving member Freddie Gillespie to the Open Space Preservation Commission following extended debate over past procedural disagreements. The board approved $30,000 in bottom-line spending from the Economic Development Committee budget for a wastewater district improvement study, while stripping a $105,000 police drone request from departmental spending. Members also reviewed a downtown wayfinding plan, received a 2027 Tricentennial update, scheduled the Fall Special Town Meeting for October 17, 2026, and set the 2027 Annual Town Meeting for March 20, 2027.

topics.title: National Grid pole petition on Parkerville Road
topics.summary: The board continued a public hearing regarding National Grid petition WR31279067 for a new pole on Parkerville Road. National Grid and town representatives reached a compromise with an abutting property owner to relocate the proposed pole roughly 1,000 feet further up the road toward the schools.
key_details: Petition WR31279067 on Parkerville Road
Pole relocated approximately 1,000 feet to an open area with no direct abutters

topics.title: Joint appointment to Library Board of Trustees
topics.summary: The Select Board met jointly with the Library Board of Trustees to fill a vacancy created by the departure of Marguerite. Molly Schofield, a volunteer with the Friends of the Southborough Library, was nominated and appointed to serve through the May 2027 town election.
key_details: Fills unexpired term of former trustee Marguerite through May 2027
Trustees board consists of six members under state law
topics.outcome: Approved 5-0 by Select Board and unanimously by Library Trustees

topics.title: Costco special act liquor license update
topics.summary: The town administrator updated the board on special legislation pending at the State House to authorize an additional off-premises liquor license for Costco. House legal counsel drafted refined language giving the town two years to award the license and a three-year sunset if it goes unused, with a legislative hearing scheduled for June 23.
key_details: Hearing scheduled before House committee June 23 from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM
Town Administrator and Chair to submit written testimony supporting the bill
Legislation grants two years to issue license, with three-year reversion to state if dormant
topics.outcome: Discussed; board agreed to submit a letter of support

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved consent agenda items, accepted a $102,500 donation from St. Mark's School for a police vehicle and general fund, approved the annual employment contract renewal for Mark Robidoux with a 3 percent salary increase, approved amended meeting minutes, and voted to enter executive session.
key_details: Accepted $102,500 donation from St. Mark's School
Approved employment contract renewal for Mark Robidoux for FY27
Approved meeting minutes for May 29, June 2, and June 8, 2026
Voted to enter executive session regarding union negotiations and minutes

topics.title: Police Department bottom-line spending and drone request
topics.summary: Police Chief Ryan Newell requested permission to use $118,000 in department and dispatch salary surplus from unfilled positions for equipment, repairs, and a five-year American-made drone program priced at $105,000. Board members supported safety gear such as AED batteries, medical bags, and cruiser ballistic plates, but objected to funding a major drone purchase through year-end operational transfers instead of vetting it through the Capital Committee and Town Meeting.
key_details: Police and dispatch surplus exceeded six figures due to vacant positions and grant funding
American-made drone system costs $105,000 under a five-year program with hardware refreshes
Board approved operational items including AED batteries and ballistic vests but removed drone
topics.why_it_matters: Ensures town equipment purchases over capital thresholds follow formal capital vetting and Town Meeting appropriation procedures rather than reallocating salary savings.

topics.title: Downtown Southborough Wayfinding Plan presentation
topics.summary: Whitney Burdge of Stantec presented the draft Downtown Southborough Wayfinding Plan funded through a state Massachusetts Downtown Initiative grant. The plan inventories 45 existing signs, categorizes directional, gateway, and informational sign typologies, and proposes a phased implementation schedule. Board members and the Historical Commission chair suggested adding omitted historic locations such as the Community House and Burnett House, while noting public preference for simpler designs.
key_details: Study inventoried 45 existing downtown signs across state, town, and private ownership
Proposed typologies include vehicular directional, pedestrian directional, and gateway signs
Town will seek Phase 2 One Stop grant funding in October to develop fabrication specs
Board will revisit sign designs and destination lists at its July 7 meeting
topics.outcome: Presentation received; board to review next steps on July 7, 2026

topics.title: Tricentennial Committee update and banner proposal
topics.summary: Tricentennial Committee Chair Don Morris and Vice Chair Patty Fiore presented an update on preparations for Southborough's 300th anniversary in 2027. Following Town Meeting approval of a sign bylaw amendment, the committee plans to install 50 decorative street banners on utility poles from August 1, 2026 through January 31, 2028, at an estimated cost of $3,500 to $5,000. Other planned activities include a January 2027 drone show, a parade, a cemetery walking tour, a summer 2027 music spectacular, tree plantings, and a brick fundraiser.
key_details: Town Meeting authorized light pole banners to remain up through January 31, 2028
Proposal calls for 50 banners across Main Street, Fayville, Cordaville, and Southville
Committee has raised over $205,000 in pledges, donations, and brick sales toward events
Committee seeks town volunteers to fill two committee vacancies and help run working groups
topics.outcome: Discussed; town administration to coordinate pole permissions with National Grid and Verizon

topics.title: Committee reappointments: Historical, Open Space, and Stewardship
topics.summary: The board addressed held committee reappointments. Kelly O'Brien declined reappointment to the Historical Commission due to relocating, which the board formally rejected 0-5. For Freddie Gillespie, the chair and members raised concerns over board consolidation goals and procedural issues from Town Meeting and developer meetings, leading the board to deny her reappointment to the Open Space Preservation Commission on a 0-5 vote despite public support. Her appointment to the Stewardship Committee was tabled pending structural clarification.
key_details: Kelly O'Brien moving out of Southborough; reappointment rejected 0-5
Freddie Gillespie denied reappointment to Open Space Preservation Commission 0-5
Board members cited committee consolidation efforts and past procedural conflicts
Public commenters urged reappointment, praising Gillespie's extensive conservation achievements
Stewardship Committee reappointment tabled to the next meeting
topics.outcome: O'Brien appointment failed 0-5; Gillespie OSPC appointment failed 0-5; Gillespie Stewardship appointment tabled
topics.why_it_matters: Removes a long-serving conservation leader from the Open Space Preservation Commission and signals Select Board scrutiny over committee alignment and town governance reform.

topics.title: Select Board office hours format
topics.summary: Board members reviewed the effectiveness of their weekly office hours, noting near-zero attendance at Town House sessions. Members agreed to move away from rigid weekday evening sessions in town hall and instead set up informational tables at public community events or offer remote Zoom availability.
key_details: Member Tim Flang reported having zero attendees at recent office hours
Board consensus to transition to event-based outreach and occasional hybrid or Zoom sessions
topics.outcome: Board agreed to reformat office hours around town events

topics.title: Wastewater Study Committee DIF financial analysis funding
topics.summary: The Wastewater Study Committee requested $30,000 in bottom-line spending from the Economic Development Committee's unused budget to engage MassDevelopment consultants. The consultants will conduct parcel-by-parcel financial and economic projections to support a District Improvement Financing (DIF) article along the Route 9 corridor at Fall Special Town Meeting.
key_details: $30,000 reallocated from Economic Development Committee salary and services surplus
MassDevelopment consultants to project incremental property tax revenues along Route 9
Intended to support defining a DIF district at the Fall Special Town Meeting
Approved 4-1 with member Andrew Pfaff dissenting over circumventing Town Meeting appropriation
topics.why_it_matters: Commits $30,000 toward economic modeling for a potential wastewater infrastructure financing district along Route 9, which could fund sewer construction using future tax growth.

topics.title: Fall Special Town Meeting and 2027 Annual Town Meeting dates
topics.summary: The board evaluated calendar conflicts and school facility availability to establish meeting dates. Members approved scheduling the Fall Special Town Meeting for Saturday, October 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM, and the 2027 Annual Town Meeting for Saturday, March 20, 2027, at 10:00 AM.
key_details: Fall Special Town Meeting set for Saturday, October 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM
Annual Town Meeting set for Saturday, March 20, 2027, at 10:00 AM
Board prioritized Saturdays to accommodate families, avoid school-night bedtimes, and assist seniors
topics.why_it_matters: Sets the dates and weekend daytime schedule for residents to debate town bylaws, appropriations, and major committee warrant articles.

topics.title: Select Board appointment to Affordable Housing Trust
topics.summary: Following the departure of Al Hamilton from the Select Board, the board appointed member Sam Stivers to serve as the Select Board representative on the Affordable Housing Trust for a one-year term.
key_details: Fills required Select Board seat on the Affordable Housing Trust
One-year term expiring June 30, 2027

votes.motion: Approve National Grid pole petition WR31279067 for Parkerville Road as relocated
Close the public hearing on National Grid pole petition WR31279067
Approve the appointment of Molly Schofield to the Library Board of Trustees through May 2027
Approve consent agenda items D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, N, and the May 29, 2026 minutes
Approve the amended minutes for June 2 and June 8, 2026
Approve the FY27 employment contract for Mark Robidoux
Approve the Police Department bottom-line spending request excluding the drone purchase
Appoint Kelly O'Brien to the Historical Commission for a term to expire June 30, 2029
Appoint Freddie Gillespie to the Open Space Preservation Commission for a five-year term expiring June 30, 2031
Approve $30,000 bottom-line spending from the Economic Development Committee budget for the Wastewater Study Committee DIF study, pending confirmation of completion prior to Fall Town Meeting
Schedule the Fall Special Town Meeting for Saturday, October 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM, and the Annual Town Meeting for Saturday, March 20, 2027, at 10:00 AM
Appoint Sam Stivers as the Select Board representative to the Affordable Housing Trust for a one-year term expiring June 30, 2027
Enter executive session under MGL c. 30A s. 21(a)(3) and (7) to discuss police detail negotiations and executive minutes, not to return to open session

public_comment.summary: A resident asked for clarification regarding the term STWO in board goal setting, which the board clarified stands for Senior Tax Work-Off.

The chair of the Historical Commission provided feedback on the wayfinding plan, urging the inclusion of omitted locations such as the Community House, Town Common, Rural Cemetery, and Burnett House, and noting that current historic district signs are readable and well-regarded.

Freddie Gillespie defended her track record and past initiatives, explaining that her Town Meeting knotweed amendment arose from sudden new legal and environmental data and apologizing for any procedural friction, while highlighting ongoing conservation projects.

The chair of the Stewardship Committee spoke in favor of reappointing Freddie Gillespie, noting her deep volunteer commitment, expertise, and essential role in active habitat restoration and meadow management projects.
A resident of Southville Road praised Freddie Gillespie's expertise and community dedication, urging the board to retain experienced volunteers and avoid personal disagreements.

upcoming.what: Legislative hearing on Costco special act liquor license bill
Select Board meeting to discuss wayfinding plan next steps and warrant items
